subject: SAML & SCIM artifacts for AuroraMed SIG review — reconciliation ask
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@auroramed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SAML & SCIM artifacts for AuroraMed SIG review — reconciliation ask

Hi Maya —

Thanks for coordinating on the SIG intake. To complete the access control section we need a few specific artifacts so our compliance reviewer can reconcile assertions against provisioning events:

- SAML assertion samples (3 examples) covering both successful and expired assertions. Prefer raw XML snippets with timestamps.
- SCIM delta/sync logs (one week window around provisioning events). CSV is fine; include header mapping.
- Role-owner matrix (CSV): list of role id, role name, owner email, last_changed_at.
- Service-account list and any delegated admin assignments.

Attach or drop to SFTP; if attaching, small CSV/XML stubs are fine. We will redact PII on our side but ask you to remove arbitrary customer identifiers.

I attached a small example export (scim-sync-sample.csv) and a placeholder SAML sample (saml-assertion-sample.xml) so you can see expected columns/fields.

High-level timeline: if we can get the artifacts by EOD Aug 21 PDT we can turn around the SIG section by Aug 24. Does that work on your side?

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Security, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com
(415) 555-0142
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@auroramed.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: security@auroramed.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 13:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SAML & SCIM artifacts for AuroraMed SIG review — reconciliation ask

Karthik —

Thanks, understood. We can provide the SCIM delta for the requested week and three SAML assertion samples. A couple quick clarifications before we drop the files:

1) For SAML assertions, do you need full raw responses (including NameID) or are time-stamped assertion elements sufficient? Our security team prefers redacting human PII fields if possible.
2) For service accounts: do you want all service principals or only those with elevated roles (admin, owner)?

We will prepare: auroramed-scim-delta-2026-07-30.csv (sample attached) and a zipped set of three assertion XMLs. We'll redact email addresses from the SAML NameID but keep tech identifiers. If you need the unredacted samples, we can SFTP them under an NDA bucket — let me know.

--
Maya Singh
Security Program Manager
AuroraMed Health
maya.singh@auroramed.com
Attachments: auroramed-scim-delta-2026-07-30.csv (CSV, 48KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@auroramed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SAML & SCIM artifacts for AuroraMed SIG review — reconciliation ask

Maya — great, thanks for the quick reply.

Answers:
- Time-stamped assertion elements are sufficient for the SIG reviewers as long as the Assertion/IssueInstant and Conditions NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter are present. Redacting NameID/email is fine; include a consistent pseudonym (e.g., user:alice@example-redacted) so we can map events.
- For service accounts, please include any accounts with roles above standard user (admin/owner/service). If it's easier, provide the full list and mark elevated ones with a role_level column.

Notes: we'll accept CSV/XML via attachment or SFTP. If you choose SFTP, please post the link to the HubSpot ticket so our ops team can fetch. I dropped a template to the shared Drive (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3ExampleLink) showing required headers for SCIM and the role-owner matrix.

Example mapping (from your attached CSV):
- scim_user_id -> scim:id
- email -> external_id (pseudonymized)
- timestamp -> meta.lastModified

If you can target EOD Aug 21 PDT that works on our side — Laura and Marcus are looped for ingestion and sanity checks.

Thanks,
Karthik

Maya — quick follow-up from intake/ingestion side:

Thanks for the sample CSV. Two small asks to make ingestion smooth:

- Please include an explicit column for scim:externalId (pseudonymized ID) — we use that to join assertion events to provisioning records.
- If you plan to SFTP, can you post credentials or a one-time link in HubSpot HS-10234? That saves time rather than email attachments for larger logs.

Timeline: if you can drop the SCIM CSV + 3 assertion XMLs by EOD Aug 21 PDT we will run an automated reconciliation (expected runtime ~4 hours) and send the reconciliation report back the morning of Aug 24. If any issues show up we'll flag required samples.

Appreciate it — Marcus
